question: Do separate Broker Supply and historical Service profiles, built without broker_response_hours, improve ranking and broker interpretability?
hypothesis: Separating what inventory a broker handles from its frozen historical outcome mix will outperform or preserve the legacy broker_profile while removing the ambiguous response-hours field.
primary_change: replace broker_profile with broker_supply_profile plus broker_service_profile
secondary_changes: historical service outcomes are frozen strictly before profile cutoff

target.censoring: Public candidate data has no true sale timestamp. scheduled_visit is the observed proxy; offline results are associative.

population.eligibility: Same population and temporal partitions as E006_physical_location_spot: profile calibration before 2025-09-29T12:58:37, predictive training until 2026-04-28T07:41:43, final 20% future test.
exclusions: Profile-calibration inquiries are excluded from predictive fitting.

validation.strategy: outcome-free profile selection on frozen calibration data + same temporal predictive train and untouched future test; paired cluster-bootstrap by lead_id
validation.split_description: Clusterers use only information available before the frozen profile cutoff. Predictive models use the identical train/test rows across arms. Bootstrap resamples lead_id clusters.

items.source: spots created before profile cutoff: sector/modality/region mix, area and price medians
pre-cutoff inquiries joined to broker: scheduled/accepted/rejected/no_response rates, asked_visit, urgency, message length, channel mix
items.information_available_at: strictly historical inquiries before profile cutoff
items.evidence: broker_response_hours is explicitly excluded; outcomes are past-only and frozen before predictive train/test.
